analysis:
The PR adds a local-only benchmark CLI mode, `--runtime-concurrency` with `--runtime-stagger`, in provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/BenchmarkCommand.swift (head lines 129-133, 312-325, 419-431). It also adds option-parsing tests and a new test file for RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark. The implementation of RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark is not in the supplied units, so it could not be reviewed.

Examined behavior:
- Argument validation runs in `benchmarkModeConflict()` before any model work. It refuses runtime options without `--runtime-generation`, `--runtime-stagger` without `--runtime-concurrency`, and malformed batch-size lists.
- Dispatch occurs only after the existing runtime-generation flow. That flow reads the prompt file with a 4 MiB cap, applies the config projection and env-conflict check, resolves KV precision, and keeps the native-block guard.
- The new path is gated behind the same `runtimeGeneration` branch. It adds no network, coordinator, WebSocket or attestation surface, and does not touch the provider keys, App Attest authorization, or prompt-cache storage in T-041.
- No prompt or consumer data is involved. The benchmark uses operator-supplied local prompts, and the report records prompt SHA-256 and token hashes, not plaintext (per the test). The runtime-generation path already prints raw tokens and text.
- The tests are test-only and add no production surface.

Remaining questions for integration:
- Whether RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.run, in a file outside this batch, keeps prefix caches off and constructs no SSD cache, as the existing runtime-generation flow does. If it enabled the SSD prefix cache it would touch T-041.
- Whether it bounds resources: batch size up to 64 with one slot per size. This is an operator-local CLI, so the DoS concern is minimal.

No security regression is identified in the supplied units.
